paper.title: Adversarially Robust Multi-Armed Bandit Algorithm with Variance-Dependent Regret Bounds

unmapped: loss minimization with loss vectors in [0,1]^K drawn i.i.d. from a joint distribution D (arms may be correlated)
settings.definition_quote: In a stochastic setting, $\ell(t) $ follows an unknown distribution $\cD$ over $[0, 1]^K$, i.i.d.~for $t = 1, 2, \ldots, T$. ... we assume that $T\ge \max\{55,K\}$ and is known to the player.

In the adversarial setting, we do not assume any generative models for the loss vector $\ell(t)$, but it can be chosen in an adversarial manner. More precisely, in each round, $\ell(t)$ may depend on the history of loss vectors and chosen arms $\{ (\ell(s), I(s)) \}_{s=1}^{t-1}$.

unmapped: corruption level defined as C = E[sum_t ||l'(t) - l(t)||_inf]; regret measured w.r.t. corrupted losses
settings.definition_quote: a \textit{temporary loss} $\ell'(t) \in [0, 1]^K$ is generated from an unknown distribution $\cD$, and the adversary then corrupts $\ell'(t)$ to determine $\ell(t)$. We define the \textit{corruption level} $C \geq 0$ by $C = \E \left[ \sum_{t=1}^T \left\|  \ell'(t) - \ell(t)  \right\|_{\infty} \right]$.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq \left( 2 (1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} \max\left\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log \left( 1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} \right), 2(1+\epsilon)\right\} \right) \log T + o (\log T)
bound.regime: bound on R(T)/log T as T -> infinity (paper states R(T) <= (...) log T + o(log T))

symbols.sigma_i: standard deviation of loss of arm i (sigma_i^2 variance)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: In any stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq ( 2 (1+\epsilon) + \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} \max\{4\frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} + c \log ( 1 + \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} ), 2(1+\epsilon)\} ) \log T + o (\log T), where ... \epsilon \in (0, 1/2] is an input parameter for the algorithm, and c = O((\log \frac{1}{\epsilon})^2).

results.notes: Recorded as limsup of R(T)/log T since theorem has o(log T) remainder. Regret R(T) = max_i E[...], which in stochastic setting equals sum Delta_i P_i (pseudo-regret). For eps=0.2 the paper gives c<=4.2 and 2(1+eps)=2.4 numerically.

symbols.h_eps: explicit piecewise function h(z) defined in eq. (defhh): 2(1+eps) for small z, else 2z(1+sqrt(1+2delta/z)) - 2delta + 4delta(log(z/(1+eps)) + log(1+sqrt(1+2delta/z))) + (1+eps)^2/z - 2(1+eps)
symbols.sigma_i: standard deviation of loss of arm i

source.label: prop:bound-sto
source.quote: In any stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves \limsup_{T \to \infty} \frac{R(T)}{\log T} \leq \sum_{i \in [K] \setminus \{ i^* \}} h ( \frac{\sigma_i^2}{\Delta_i} ) + 2 \bet

results.notes: Refined form of Theorem 1 stochastic bound; h is a complicated explicit function, abbreviated as symbol.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Further, in adversarial settings, the regret for the proposed algorithm satisfies R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\left\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \right\}} + O(K \log T)

results.notes: Worst-case instance of the min (taking T). Leading constant is exactly 1 on sqrt(K T log T); only the additive K log T term is in O.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\left\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \right\}} + O(K \log T)

symbols.L_star: L^* = min_i E[sum_t ell_i(t)], cumulative loss of best arm
symbols.Q_inf: Q_infty = min_{bar ell} E[sum_t ||ell(t) - bar ell||_inf^2], loss variation

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: R(T) \leq \sqrt{K \log T \min\left\{ T, 4L^*,  4 (T-L^*),  4 Q_{\infty}  \right\}} + O(K \log T) for L^* = \min_{i^* \in [K] }\E [ \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{i^*} (t) ] and Q_{\infty} = \min_{\bar{\ell} \in [0,1]^K} \E [ \sum_{t=1}^T \|\ell_i(t) - \bar{\ell}\|_{\infty}^2 ].

results.notes: Data-dependent (first-order and second-order) bound; leading term has explicit constant, additive term O(K log T).

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound (2(1+eps) + sum_subopt max{4 sigma_i^2/Delta_i + c log(1+sigma_i^2/Delta_i), 2(1+eps)}) log T + o(log T)

source.label: prop:bound-corrupted
source.quote: In any corrupted stochastic setting with a unique optimal arm, the proposed algorithm achieves R(T) \leq \mathcal{R} + O ( \sqrt{C \mathcal{R}} ), where \mathcal{R} is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto} and C is the corruption level defined in Section~\ref{sec:setting}.

results.notes: Only the corruption term is in O; R_sto itself has explicit leading constant. Regret defined w.r.t. corrupted losses.

source.label: prop_moment
source.quote: For any $0\le \mu^*<\mu_i\le 1$ and $\sigma_i^2 \le \mu_i(1-\mu_i)$, there exists a loss distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $[0,1]^K$ such that any consistent algorithm suffers \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{R(T)}{\log T} \ge \sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{\Delta_i}{...} and there exists an algorithm achieving this bound with equality for all $\mathcal{D}$.

results.notes: Simplification of Honda & Takemura (2012) Theorem 4; the paper derives the closed form. Approximately sum (2 sigma_i^2/Delta_i + 0.5 log(1+sigma_i^2/Delta_i) + 1) within 6% relative error after sup over mu.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{K}{1-2\eta} \left( \min\left\{ T, 4 L^*, 4 (T - L^*), 4 Q_{\infty}, \frac{8}{\eta} V_1 \right\} + \frac{K}{\eta} \right) \log T } + O(K \log T)

symbols.eta: input parameter of modified algorithm in (0,1/2)

source.quote: by modifying the algorithm in the way described in Appendix~\ref{sec:path-length}, we can obtain a regret bound of R(T) \leq \sqrt{ \frac{K}{1-2\eta} ( \min\{ T, 4 L^*, 4 (T - L^*), 4 Q_{\infty}, \frac{8}{\eta} V_1 \} + \frac{K}{\eta} ) \log T } + O(K \log T) in adversarial settings, where $\eta \in (0, 1 / 2 )$ is an input parameter.

results.notes: Stated in a remark with proof sketch in Appendix C.

symbols.R_sto: RHS of the stochastic bound of Theorem 1

source.quote: In corrupted stochastic settings, this modified algoirthm achieves a regret bound of R(T) \leq  \frac{1}{1-2\eta} \mathcal{R} + O ( \sqrt{ \frac{1}{1-2\eta} C \mathcal{R} } + K \sqrt{\frac{ \log T }{\eta (1-2\eta)}} ), where \mathcal{R} is the RHS of \eqref{eq:thm1-bound-sto}.

results.notes: Leading term R_sto/(1-2eta) has explicit constant; remaining terms in O.
